Passed 2026-04-06. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This law prohibits a person who develops or deploys an artificial intelligence system from advertising or representing to the public that the system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional. A violation is treated as an unfair or deceptive act or practice under the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977 and is subject to a civil penalty of five thousand dollars per violation. The law defines artificial intelligence and takes effect July 1, 2026.

Who it applies to

  • A person who develops or deploys an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a))

Effective date

July 1, 2026 (Sec. 3)

Key definitions

  • artificial intelligence: models and systems capable of performing functions generally associated with human intelligence, including reasoning and learning (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(c))

Prohibitions

  • A person who develops or deploys an artificial intelligence system shall not advertise or represent to the public that such system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a))

Penalties and enforcement

A violation of the prohibition constitutes a violation of the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977, compiled in title 47, chapter 18, part 1. It constitutes an unfair or deceptive act or practice affecting trade or commerce and is subject to the penalties and remedies provided in that Act. Notwithstanding the civil penalty limits provided by the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977, a violation is subject to a civil penalty of five thousand dollars per violation. The text does not state a private right of action or a specific enforcement agency beyond the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977 (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(b)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying an artificial intelligence system must ensure that its advertising and public representations do not state or imply that the system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a)).
  • If the organisation violates this prohibition, it may be subject to a civil penalty of five thousand dollars per violation and other penalties and remedies under the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977 (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(b)).
  • The organisation should review all marketing materials, product descriptions, and public statements about the AI system to remove any claims of qualified mental health professional status (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a)).

Compliance steps

  • Review all advertising and public representations for the artificial intelligence system to identify any statements that the system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a)).
  • Remove or revise any such statements so that the system is not advertised or represented as a qualified mental health professional (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a)).
  • Train employees and contractors involved in marketing or deployment to avoid making claims that the AI system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a)).
  • Monitor ongoing advertising and public representations to ensure continued compliance with the prohibition (Sec. 1, § 33-1-205(a)).

 PUBLIC CHAPTER NO. 647
 SENATE BILL NO.1580

 By Walley, Crowe, Yarbro, Reeves

 Substituted for: House Bill No. 1470

 By Tim Hicks, Reneau, Powell, Salinas, Garringer

AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 33; Title 47 and Title 63, relative to mental
 health.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 33, Chapter 1, Part 2, is amended by adding
the following as a new section:

 33-1-205.

 (a) A person who develops or deploys an artificial intelligence system shall not
 advertise or represent to the public that such system is or is able to act as a qualified mental
 health professional.

 (b) A violation of subsection (a) constitutes a violation of the Tennessee Consumer
 Protection Act of 1977, compiled in title 47, chapter 18, part 1. A violation of subsection (a)
 constitutes an unfair or deceptive act or practice affecting trade or commerce and is subject
 to the penalties and remedies provided in the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977.
 Notwithstanding the civil penalty limits provided by the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act
 of 1977, a violation of subsection (a) is subject to a civil penalty of five thousand dollars
 ($5,000) per violation.

 (c) As used in this section, "artificial intelligence" means models and systems capable
 of performing functions generally associated with human intelligence, including reasoning
 and learning.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 47-18-104(b), is amended by adding the
following as a new subdivision:

 ( ) Violating § 33-1-205;

 SECTION 3. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
  SENATE BILL NO. 1580
